PASS on the fake backend, final gate run. Served device mhs://localhost/openarm-bimanual, kind world.sim, mode simulated, risk R0 (the card's floor, and the floor of cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1). The model is the card's models[0], v1/scene.xml, read in place from the pinned clone (robots/enactic/openarm_mujoco/v1/scene.xml; never copied, imported, installed or modified). It includes v1/openarm_bimanual.xml: 16 position actuators (eight per arm), 18 qpos and 18 dof, timestep 0.001 s, implicitfast. The bridge derives action.ctrl's per-actuator bounds from each actuator's ctrlrange (left arm at 548-554, right arm at 556-562, fingers through the motor_finger default at 41-45); the package writes no Limit of its own. The fake backend is fake.py, a callable stand-in mujoco module that parses the same MJCF and integrates a placeholder first-order motion, so the gate warns G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND (there is no package fake class surface for the family to record) and G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the family-derived inputs ticks, action.ctrl[*] and the reset seed; these are the expected simulator-family warnings. G4 had no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warnings. NOT COVERED: the MuJoCo engine was not installed and was never run; the fake computes no inertias, contacts, tendons, finger equalities or actuator dynamics, so its trajectories are not MuJoCo results; the v1/meshes assets are not loaded by the stand-in; cap.world.reset.v1 calls mj_resetData and does not apply the home keyframe; no rendering, cameras or sensor streams are served; no physical OpenArm is modelled or driven and no hardware run is claimed. Snapshot/restore is advertised through the bridge and declared in fidelity, but it is not covered by the CL3 gate; an in-process restore of the snapshot returned by mhs.snapshot was rejected with MHS.CONFLICT.STATE_HASH because the bridge's snapshot document (integration_state) differs from the read state whose hash the server stores. That is an SDK-layer observation, not a driver result, and it is not presented as an engine or hardware validation. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null).
